_what: Claim-level adjudication of the nine stage-0 declarations, per the rubric pre-registered at the rubric in evidence/METHOD.md. Clusters group claims across arms that answer the same design question; verdicts follow the mechanical criteria: fork = different interface/signal/shape or same shape with a constant differing >=2x; same = wording or incidental detail; complementary = disjoint non-conflicting aspects. Retro-tagging is ADJUDICATOR-APPLIED, not arm-declared. Adjudicator wrote the briefs, read the real fixes, and saw stage-0's numbers; every verdict therefore quotes its evidence so it can be re-run by a disagreeing reader.
lc_primary_note: least_confident consensus maps each referenced claim to the single cluster where it is that arm's principal statement; the mapping is recorded per cluster in 'lc_members'.

t1-reveal.question: How is reveal performed?
t1-reveal.justification: All three: org.freedesktop.FileManager1.ShowItems via CLI shell-out (no dbus crate), degrade to opening the containing directory. CLI try-order differs (a/b: dbus-send first; c: gdbus first, no busctl leg) - same interface, same chain structure, incidental order.

t1-reveal.question: Where does the reveal errand execute?
t1-reveal.justification: All three: a spawned std::thread does the waiting; the UI thread never blocks. c frames it as 'throwaway thread that waits' vs open_with_system's detached process - same runtime behaviour.

t1-reveal.question: Which file:// authorities count as local?
t1-reveal.justification: All three: empty or 'localhost' only; any other host refused.

t1-reveal.question: Malformed %-escapes?
t1-reveal.justification: All three decode malformed escapes literally rather than rejecting the link.

t1-reveal.question: Non-UTF-8 bytes in a decoded path?
t1-reveal.justification: a: 'byte-level %XX decoding into an OsString so spaces and non-UTF-8 names survive'. b: 'non-UTF-8 decodes are refused'. c: 'strict-UTF-8 percent-decoder... non-UTF-8 rejected'. Different data shape (OsString vs String), materially different behaviour on non-UTF-8 names.

t1-reveal.question: query/fragment on a printed file:// URI?
t1-reveal.justification: a: 'query/fragment are NOT stripped... likelier a literal character of a filename'. c: '?query/#fragment are stripped'. Opposite handling; file:///x#y resolves to different targets. b silent.

t1-reveal.question: Outgoing URI percent-encoding alphabet?
t1-reveal.justification: a and c: escape everything outside unreserved+'/' specifically to stay inert in dbus-send/gdbus grammars; b commits to a hand-rolled encoder without stating the alphabet - no conflict.

t1-reveal.question: How is the reveal target classified and gated?
t1-reveal.justification: All three: a pure classifier over the existing link machinery, gated on the decoded path existing on disk, shared by chord and menu. c's link_token_under/reveal_path_under split is factoring, not behaviour.

t1-reveal.question: Chord placement and fall-through?
t1-reveal.justification: All three: Super+Ctrl checked before the Shift/Ctrl open chord because it contains Ctrl; non-revealable targets fall through to the ordinary open.

t1-reveal.question: Localise the context-menu row?
t1-reveal.justification: All three: hardcoded English, matching the menu's unlocalised siblings.

t1-reveal.question: Help-modal discoverability?
t1-reveal.justification: All three: a LINKS-section row, new strings across all nine language tables, self-written translations.

t1-reveal.question: Changelog entry?
t1-reveal.justification: b and c both add an Unreleased/Added entry; a wrote none and declared none (visible in the file-grain metric as the only file-set difference).

t2-adoption.question: What rule demotes a trivial session?
t2-adoption.justification: a: 'handicapped save time, not an absolute tier'. b: 'one tier between the workspace hint and recency... still in play... within SUBSTANCE_WINDOW'. c: 'effective save time rather than a hard tier'. Handicap (a,c) vs bounded tier (b) are different control structures with observably different orderings (e.g. a 2-day-old wall vs a 1-day-old throwaway).

t2-adoption.question: The demotion constant
t2-adoption.justification: a: TRIVIAL_HANDICAP = 72h. c: TRIVIAL_HANDICAP = 7 days. b: SUBSTANCE_WINDOW = 7 days. 72h vs 168h = 2.33x >= 2x - fork by the constant rule even between the two same-shape arms.

t2-adoption.question: What counts as trivial?
t2-adoption.justification: All three: panes <= 1 is trivial; two panes is already arranged.

t2-adoption.question: How is substance recorded?
t2-adoption.justification: All three: a top-level `panes = N` scalar written beside last_workspace at save time from the existing pane_count().

t2-adoption.question: How is the count read on scan?
t2-adoption.justification: All three: extend the hand-rolled stop-at-first-table line scanner off the single read_to_string the scan already does; no deserialisation. a's shared-helper refactor is factoring.

t2-adoption.question: Unknown pane count ranks as?
t2-adoption.justification: All three: missing key reads as substantial/arranged, so pre-upgrade files are never demoted - the polarity choice.

t2-adoption.question: Workspace-hint precedence?
t2-adoption.justification: All three: the hint stays the untouched first key; the new rule operates only beneath it.

t2-adoption.question: Does the scratch-window theme borrow share the rank?
t2-adoption.justification: All three: keep resolve_key/theme_key_in on the shared rank() - 'one ranking doctrine rather than two'.

t2-adoption.question: How is the writer/scanner coupling verified?
t2-adoption.justification: a and b both pin, by test, that toml 0.8 emits the top-level hints ahead of the first table header. c's test list does not include the serialisation-order pin.

t3-bell.question: What does a BEL become?
t3-bell.justification: All three demote the BEL from trigger to claim: it parks/arms/defers and something else corroborates before any announcement.

t3-bell.question: Working-agent suppression and the idle hold (bug 1)
t3-bell.justification: All three: judge against the offset-immune live-screen thinking probe; ring only after the same 300ms idle hold the scan's debounce uses; a and c both explicitly skip the 1200ms real-spell test on the bell path.

t3-bell.question: How long does a parked claim survive continued work?
t3-bell.justification: a: observed thinking voids the claim at the next adjudication tick (~120ms). b: expires at 10s. c: discards at 5s. Ratios far beyond 2x, and void-immediately vs grace-period is a different shape.

t3-bell.question: Restore-burst suppression signal (bug 2)
t3-bell.justification: Three different signals. a: input provenance - 'a BEL arms only when human_typed is set, which only send() sets'. b: observation history - 'parks only if the pane observed its agent working within the last 30s'. c: spawn age plus evidence - '10s BELL_SPAWN_GRACE... plus an evidence gate (cached thinking, or the working-to-idle flip within 5s)'.

t3-bell.question: A repeat BEL while a finish is latched?
t3-bell.justification: All three: swallowed/ignored rather than re-ringing; pending state cleared so an acked finish cannot re-announce.

t3-bell.question: How is the scan path kept unchanged?
t3-bell.justification: Different refactors (shared ring_finish; hoisted probe consuming the same-tick value; seeded not_thinking_since with the scan's ring inert), identical commitment: scan-path behaviour preserved exactly.

t3-bell.question: Where does the decision logic live and how is it tested?
t3-bell.justification: All three extract pure verdict functions beside wants_human/looks_blocked and table-test them; live-PTY scenarios declared untestable rather than faked.
